texts.preamble: Kutbuddin M Hussain vs Food And Drugs Administration on 7 March, 2019 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh, Bench At Indore Criminal Revision No.650 Of 2019 Indore, Dated 07.03.2019 Mr. Ankit Premchandani, Counsel for the applicants.
texts.facts: The applicants had originally filed criminal revision under Section 397 read with 401 of Cr.P.C. against the order passed in Criminal Appeal No.60/2018 by the Court of Sessions Judge, Badwani which was a matter pertaining to Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Consequently an application has been filed to convert the present criminal revision into Misc. Appeal.
texts.arguments: Counsel for the non-applicant/State has submitted that the applicants have not been sentenced to fine, but has been inflicted with penalty which cannot be suspended as 'penalty' is not 'sentenced'. Counsel for the applicants submitted that he shall demonstrate that penalty which has been imposed upon the applicants was infact sentence. Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted a citation of Allahabad High Court in the case of Pradeep Kumar Gupta v/s State of U.P. [Criminal Appeal No.1586 of 2015 decided on 12.05.2015] in which criminal appeal preferred under Section 71 (6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been allowed to be converted into Civil Misc. Appeal and it has been ordered that the appeal be de-registered as criminal appeal and re-registered as Misc. Appeal. The learned counsel submits that it would be appropriate Court's action to do likewise by this Court as well.
texts.petitioner_arguments: Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted a citation of Allahabad High Court in the case of Pradeep Kumar Gupta v/s State of U.P. [Criminal Appeal No.1586 of 2015 decided on 12.05.2015] in which criminal appeal preferred under Section 71 (6) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been allowed to be converted into Civil Misc. Appeal and it has been ordered that the appeal be de-registered as criminal appeal and re-registered as Misc. Appeal. The learned counsel submits that it would be appropriate Court's action to do likewise by this Court as well.
texts.respondent_arguments: Counsel for the non-applicant/State has submitted that the applicants have not been sentenced to fine, but has been inflicted with penalty which cannot be suspended as 'penalty' is not 'sentenced'. Counsel for the applicants submitted that he shall demonstrate that penalty which has been imposed upon the applicants was infact sentence.
